subject: Social Studies
stem: Sikhism, a monotheistic religion emphasising equality, devotion to one God, and rejection of caste distinctions, was founded in the 15th century in the Punjab region by:
explanation: Guru Nanak (1469-1539), the first of the ten Sikh Gurus, founded Sikhism preaching one formless God and social equality — Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, later institutionalised the Khalsa Panth, while Kabir was a separate, roughly contemporary Bhakti-movement poet-saint who influenced but did not found Sikhism.
